Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. === test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7244_thank-you_sent_on_job_completion_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story853.Criterion7244Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 853 — Leave a review when the job is done well
  Criterion 7244 — Thank-you sent on job completion

  Mirrors story 836's criterion 7153 for driving the real "mark
  complete" flow on `FieldLive.Job`. Assumes a thank-you email whose
  subject contains "thank" (`CleanerCrm.Reviews`'s `ReviewNotifier`,
  by analogy with `ReceiptNotifier`/`ReminderNotifier`).
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "completing a job sends the client an immediate thank-you" do
    scenario "thank-you sent on job completion" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has a scheduled job", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{status: :scheduled})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client immediately receives a thank-you note", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email, subject: ~r/thank/i)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

=== test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7245_review_request_sent_24h_after_completion_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story853.Criterion7245Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 853 — Leave a review when the job is done well
  Criterion 7245 — Review request sent ~24h after completion

  The automatic ~24h-later trigger has no user-facing action to drive
  — the spec cannot call `CleanerCrm.Reviews` directly (sealed
  boundary). Mirrors story 837's criterion 7183: rather than backdate
  any row's own timestamp, `Fixtures.run_due_review_requests/1` runs
  the periodic scan with an explicit "as of" time 24 hours after the
  job was completed, the same injectable-`now` seam
  `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send/1` already
  uses in production.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a review request goes out roughly a day after the visit is completed" do
    scenario "review request sent ~24h after completion" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client's visit was just completed", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{status: :scheduled})

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "roughly 24 hours pass", context do
        as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
        Fixtures.run_due_review_requests(as_of)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client receives a review request", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email, subject: ~r/review/i)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

=== test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7246_no_duplicate_review_request_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story853.Criterion7246Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 853 — Leave a review when the job is done well
  Criterion 7246 — No duplicate review request

  The request send itself is covered by criterion 7245's spec; this
  spec's subject is the scan's idempotency once a request has already
  gone out, so the already-sent request is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.review_request_fixture/4`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the review-request scan never sends a second request for the same visit" do
    scenario "no duplicate review request" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a completed visit already had its review request sent", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)
        Fixtures.review_request_fixture(context.scope, job, client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the review-request scan runs again a day later", context do
        as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 48 * 60 * 60, :second)
        Fixtures.run_due_review_requests(as_of)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "no second review request is sent", context do
        refute_email_sent()

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story853.Criterion7247Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 853 — Leave a review when the job is done well
  Criterion 7247 — High rating routes to publish

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Booking,
              CleanerCrm.Portal,
              CleanerCrm.Reviews
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Client portal (stories 851, 852) — an already-established client
  # portal session.
  #
  # The magic-link exchange itself (`/portal/access/:token`) is covered
  # end-to-end by story 850's own specs. Downstream portal stories
  # whose subject is what a client can do once inside the portal seed
  # the session directly here instead of re-driving that exchange
  # every time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  # Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth` reads the client id from the
  # `:portal_client_id` session key (mirroring `:user_token` for staff
  # auth).
  def portal_session_fixture(client) do
    Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  # Reschedule/cancel policy (story 851) — the account's configured
  # notice window and fees.
  #
  # The client-facing decision (on-time, late, or same-day) is the
  # subject under test, so this only seeds the account's stated
  # policy, never a per-job fee outcome.
  def cancellation_policy_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, policy} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.set_cancellation_policy(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })
      )

    policy
  end

  # Quoting (story 848) — the account's public-facing rate card, set
  # directly rather than through the office `QuoteLive.Builder` rate
  # card form (covered end-to-end by story 835) since these specs'
  # subject is the public instant-quote calculator reading it, not the
  # office save flow. Extra keys the current `RateCard` schema doesn't
  # persist yet (frequency discounts, add-on pricing) are accepted
  # here so specs can drive the pricing config story 848 needs once
  # the schema grows to hold it.
  def rate_card_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    rate_card = CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
    {:ok, rate_card} = CleanerCrm.Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, attrs)
    rate_card
  end

  # Booking (story 849) — an instant quote already accepted by the
  # client (contact captured, price locked). The quote-to-accepted
  # transition itself is covered end-to-end by story 848's own
  # "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" spec, so
  # scenarios whose subject is the slot/policy/card steps that follow
  # seed the accepted lead directly here instead of re-driving the
  # quote calculator every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      CleanerCrm.Booking.create_lead(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  # Portal (story 850) — an already-issued, not-yet-exchanged
  # magic-link token for a client, distinct from `portal_session_fixture/1`
  # above (which bypasses straight to an established session for
  # downstream stories 851/852). This one's subject is the token
  # exchange itself — validity and expiry — so it hands back the raw
  # session/token record rather than a conn already carrying it.
  def portal_magic_link_fixture(client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, session} = CleanerCrm.Portal.create_portal_session(client, Enum.into(attrs, %{}))
    session
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — an already-sent review request for a
  # completed visit, distinct from the thank-you/request send itself
  # (covered end-to-end by criteria 7244/7245's own specs). Scenarios
  # whose subject is what happens once the client reaches
  # `ReviewLive.Public` (rating routing, no-duplicate-request) seed
  # the already-requested review directly here instead of re-driving
  # the completion-to-request pipeline every time — a sanctioned
  # shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def review_request_fixture(scope, job, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, review} =
      CleanerCrm.Reviews.create_review(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          client_id: client.id,
          status: :review_requested,
          token: "review_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        })
      )

    review
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — runs the periodic review-request scan now,
  # exactly as `CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewScheduler.perform/1` does on
  # its Oban cron schedule (mirrors `send_due_reminders/0` above for
  # story 837's reminder scan). `as_of` lets a spec assert the
  # ~24h-later trigger without backdating any row's own timestamp —
  # the same injectable "now" seam `ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send/1`
  # already uses.
  def run_due_review_requests(as_of \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    CleanerCrm.Reviews.send_due_review_requests(as_of)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
  @moduledoc """
  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.

  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
  a job is created.

  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
  an account that hasn't opted in.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications

  import Ecto.Query
  require Logger

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
    scan_and_send()
    :ok
  end

  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    ReminderSettings
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
  end

  defp send_for_account(
         %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours},
         now
       ) do
    account_id
    |> due_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder_isolated/1)
  end

  # One job's send failing (a delivery-adapter bug, a bad email
  # address, whatever) must never stop the rest of the scan — each job
  # gets its own failure boundary rather than the whole `Enum.each`
  # aborting on the first raise.
  defp send_reminder_isolated(job) do
    send_reminder(job)
  rescue
    error ->
      Logger.error(
        "ReminderScheduler failed to send reminder for job #{job.id}: " <>
          Exception.format(:error, error, __STACKTRACE__)
      )
  end

  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
    already_reminded =
      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder

    from(j in Job,
      as: :job,
      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
      where: j.status == :scheduled,
      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
      where: not exists(already_reminded),
      preload: [:client]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp due_now?(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}, lead_time_hours, now) do
    with {:ok, start_at} <- DateTime.new(date, time, "Etc/UTC") do
      due_at = DateTime.add(start_at, -lead_time_hours * 3600, :second)
      DateTime.compare(due_at, now) != :gt and DateTime.compare(start_at, now) == :gt
    else
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: %Client{preferred_channel: :sms, phone: phone}} = job)
       when is_binary(phone) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    body = reminder_sms_body(job, token)

    case Delivery.send_sms(phone, body) do
      {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}} ->
        insert_notification!(job, job.client, :sms, token, sid, DateTime.utc_now())

      {:error, _reason} ->
        send_email_reminder(job, job.client)
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: client} = job), do: send_email_reminder(job, client)

  defp send_email_reminder(job, client) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    insert_notification!(job, client, :email, token, nil, DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp reminder_sms_body(job, token) do
    "Cleaning appointment reminder for #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. " <>
      "Confirm: #{reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")} " <>
      "Reschedule: #{reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")}"
  end

  defp insert_notification!(job, client, channel, token, provider_message_id, sent_at) do
    %Notification{account_id: job.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: channel,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      provider_message_id: provider_message_id,
      sent_at: sent_at
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderNotifier do @moduledoc """ Builds and delivers the appointment reminder email via `CleanerCrm.Mailer` (Swoosh/Resend). Every reminder — whether sent on the client's preferred channel or as the SMS-undeliverable fallback — carries both the confirm and reschedule links. """ import Swoosh.Email alias CleanerCrm.Mailer alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job def deliver_reminder(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job, confirm_url, reschedule_url) do client.email |> reminder_email(job, confirm_url, reschedule_url) |> Mailer.deliver() end defp reminder_email(to, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url) do new() |> to(to) |> from({"CleanerCrm", "contact@example.com"}) |> subject("Reminder: your cleaning appointment on #{job.scheduled_date}") |> html_body("""

This is a reminder about your cleaning appointment on \ #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}.

Confirm this appointment

Request a reschedule

""") |> text_body(""" Reminder: your cleaning appointment is on #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. Confirm: #{confirm_url} Reschedule: #{reschedule_url} """) end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent do @moduledoc """ A job's checklist, grouped by room, with live progress and a gate on job completion until every required item is checked or explicitly skipped with a reason. "Still needed before this job is done" is recomputed from the checklist on every update, not cached from the last failed completion attempt — so it clears live the moment a cleaner checks off (or skips) the last required item, without needing to press "Finish Job" again. Skipping asks for a reason inline (its own `
`, scoped to that item) rather than hardcoding one; the reason is persisted on the `ChecklistItem` for `QualityLive.Review` to show the owner. Each item renders as its own `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent` so its before/after photo uploads stay independently scoped. Completing the job also generates its invoice, when `CleanerCrm.Billing` is present — read defensively per the moduledoc note on `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2` about that hook not existing yet everywhere it's called from. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-------------------|----------|----------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | the checklist's job (for billing) | | checklist | `Checklist.t()` | yes | the job's checklist, items preloaded | Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :job_completed)` once the job is marked complete, so it can reload the job and checklist. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quality` - `CleanerCrm.Billing` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Billing alias CleanerCrm.Quality alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Checklist

{elem(@progress, 0)} of {elem(@progress, 1)}

{room}

    <.live_component :for={item <- items} module={ChecklistItemComponent} id={"checklist-item-#{item.id}"} current_scope={@current_scope} item={item} />

Still needed before this job is done:

  • {item.task}
<.button :if={is_nil(@checklist.completed_at)} data-test="mark-complete-button" phx-click="mark_complete" phx-target={@myself} class="mt-3" > Finish Job
""" end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:rooms, Quality.group_by_room(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:progress, Quality.progress(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:incomplete, Quality.incomplete_required_items(assigns.checklist)) |> assign_new(:skip_form_item_id, fn -> nil end)} end @impl true def handle_event("mark_complete", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Quality.complete_job(scope, socket.assigns.checklist) do {:ok, _completed} -> maybe_generate_invoice(scope, socket.assigns.job) send(self(), :job_completed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, [])} {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, incomplete)} end end def handle_event("show_skip_form", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, item_id)} end def handle_event("cancel_skip_form", _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} end def handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id, "reason" => reason}, socket) do item = Enum.find(socket.assigns.checklist.items, &(&1.id == item_id)) case Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, reason) do {:ok, _item} -> send(self(), :checklist_changed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, socket} end end # Not every account has `CleanerCrm.Billing` wired to this hook yet # (see its moduledoc) — read defensively so this component never # needs to change again once it lands. defp maybe_generate_invoice(scope, job) do if Code.ensure_loaded?(Billing) and function_exported?(Billing, :generate_for_job, 2) do Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job) end end end

1 defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job do 2 @moduledoc """ 3 A single job workspace: the room-by-room checklist, clock in/out 4 with running earnings, and incident reporting. 5 6 Route: `/field/jobs/:id`. A cleaner who opens a job not assigned to 7 them is redirected straight back to `/field` with a flash — the 8 page exposes entry codes and client details, so an unassigned 9 cleaner must never see it render at all (reconciled with story 10 838's criterion 7123 and story 844's criterion 7129). Office staff 11 (an account's `:owner`/`:admin`) can open any job in the account, 12 assigned or not — story 836's criterion 7153 exercises exactly that, 13 completing a job that was never assigned to a specific cleaner. 14 15 ## Dependencies 16 17 - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` 18 - `CleanerCrm.Quality` 19 - `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` 20 - `CleanerCrm.Accounts` — only to distinguish office staff from a 21 field cleaner for the check above. 22 - `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent` 23 - `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.IncidentFormComponent` 24 """ 25 26 use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view 27 28 alias CleanerCrm.Accounts 29 alias CleanerCrm.Money 30 alias CleanerCrm.Quality 31 alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling 32 alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking 33 alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, TimeEntry} 34 alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.{ChecklistComponent, IncidentFormComponent} 35 36 @impl true 37 def render(assigns) do 38 ~H""" 39 40
41 <.header> 42 {client_name(@job)} 43 <:subtitle> 44 {@job.scheduled_date} · {format_time(@job.start_time)}–{format_time(@job.end_time)} 45 46 <:actions> 47 Complete 48 49 50 51
52
53

54 You're still clocked in to your {@clock_in_warning.client && 55 @clock_in_warning.client.name} job — clock out there first. 56

57 58
59 Clocked in 60 {format_duration(@elapsed_seconds)} 61 <.button data-test="clock-out-button" phx-click="clock_out">Clock Out 62
63 64

69 Missing clock-out — remember to clock out when you're done. 70

71 72
73 Clocked out 74 75 {format_duration(@last_worked_seconds)} 76 77 <.button data-test="clock-in-button" phx-click="clock_in">Clock In 78
79 80

81 {Money.format_cents(@earnings_cents)} 82

83
84
85 86 <.live_component 87 module={ChecklistComponent} 88 id="checklist" 89 current_scope={@current_scope} 90 job={@job} 91 checklist={@checklist} 92 /> 93 94 <.live_component 95 module={IncidentFormComponent} 96 id="incident-form" 97 current_scope={@current_scope} 98 job={@job} 99 /> 100
101 102 """ 103 end 104 105 @impl true 106 def mount(%{"id" => id}, _session, socket) do 107 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 108 job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, id) 109 110 if assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job) or office_staff?(scope) do 111 {:ok, 112 socket 113 |> assign(:job, job) 114 |> assign(:page_title, "Job") 115 |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) 116 |> load_checklist() 117 |> load_time_state() 118 |> maybe_schedule_tick()} 119 else 120 {:ok, 121 socket 122 |> put_flash(:error, "This job is not assigned to you.") 123 |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")} 124 end 125 end 126 127 @impl true 128 def handle_event("clock_in", _params, socket) do 129 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 130 job = socket.assigns.job 131 132 case TimeTracking.clock_in(scope, job) do 133 {:ok, _entry} -> 134 {:noreply, socket |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) |> load_time_state()} 135 136 {:error, {:already_clocked_in, other_job}} -> 137 {:noreply, assign(socket, :clock_in_warning, Scheduling.get_job!(scope, other_job.id))} 138 139 {:error, _reason} -> 140 {:noreply, socket} 141 end 142 end 143 144 def handle_event("clock_out", _params, socket) do 145 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 146 job = socket.assigns.job 147 148 case TimeTracking.clock_out(scope, job) do 149 {:ok, _entry} -> {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} 150 {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket} 151 end 152 end 153 154 @impl true 155 def handle_info(:job_completed, socket) do 156 job = Scheduling.get_job!(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job.id) 157 {:noreply, socket |> assign(:job, job) |> load_checklist()} 158 end 159 160 def handle_info(:checklist_changed, socket), do: {:noreply, load_checklist(socket)} 161 162 def handle_info(:tick, socket) do 163 if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) 164 {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} 165 end 166 167 defp maybe_schedule_tick(socket) do 168 if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) 169 socket 170 end 171 172 defp assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job), do: job.cleaner_id == scope.user.id 173 174 defp office_staff?(scope) do 175 case scope.active_account_id do 176 nil -> false 177 account_id -> Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin] 178 end 179 end 180 181 # Every job gets a checklist to complete through, even a trivially 182 # empty one for a job nothing ever assigned a template to — lazily 183 # instantiated here so `ChecklistComponent`'s completion flow (and 184 # the invoice it triggers) is the one path every job completes 185 # through, rather than a second one this view would otherwise need 186 # for the no-checklist case. 187 defp load_checklist(socket) do 188 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 189 job = socket.assigns.job 190 191 checklist = 192 case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do 193 nil -> 194 {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, []) 195 checklist 196 197 checklist -> 198 checklist 199 end 200 201 assign(socket, :checklist, checklist) 202 end 203 204 defp load_time_state(socket) do 205 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 206 job = socket.assigns.job 207 entries = TimeTracking.list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job) 208 last_resolved = entries |> Enum.filter(&TimeEntry.resolved?/1) |> List.last() 209 210 socket 211 |> assign(:open_entry, TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job)) 212 |> assign(:elapsed_seconds, TimeTracking.elapsed_seconds(scope, job)) 213 |> assign(:last_worked_seconds, last_resolved && Earnings.worked_seconds(last_resolved)) 214 |> assign(:earnings_cents, TimeTracking.job_earnings_cents(scope, job)) 215 end 216 217 defp client_name(%{client: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name 218 defp client_name(%{property: %{client: %{name: name}}}) when is_binary(name), do: name 219 defp client_name(_job), do: "Job" 220 221 defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-H:%M") 222 223 defp format_duration(nil), do: "0m" 224 225 defp format_duration(seconds) do 226 hours = div(seconds, 3600) 227 minutes = div(rem(seconds, 3600), 60) 228 "#{hours}h #{minutes}m" 229 end 230 end 231

<.header> {client_name(@job)} <:subtitle> {@job.scheduled_date} · {format_time(@job.start_time)}–{format_time(@job.end_time)} <:actions> Complete

You're still clocked in to your {@clock_in_warning.client && @clock_in_warning.client.name} job — clock out there first.

Clocked in {format_duration(@elapsed_seconds)} <.button data-test="clock-out-button" phx-click="clock_out">Clock Out

Missing clock-out — remember to clock out when you're done.

Clocked out {format_duration(@last_worked_seconds)} <.button data-test="clock-in-button" phx-click="clock_in">Clock In

{Money.format_cents(@earnings_cents)}

<.live_component module={ChecklistComponent} id="checklist" current_scope={@current_scope} job={@job} checklist={@checklist} /> <.live_component module={IncidentFormComponent} id="incident-form" current_scope={@current_scope} job={@job} />
""" end @impl true def mount(%{"id" => id}, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, id) if assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job) or office_staff?(scope) do {:ok, socket |> assign(:job, job) |> assign(:page_title, "Job") |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) |> load_checklist() |> load_time_state() |> maybe_schedule_tick()} else {:ok, socket |> put_flash(:error, "This job is not assigned to you.") |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")} end end @impl true def handle_event("clock_in", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job case TimeTracking.clock_in(scope, job) do {:ok, _entry} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) |> load_time_state()} {:error, {:already_clocked_in, other_job}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :clock_in_warning, Scheduling.get_job!(scope, other_job.id))} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket} end end def handle_event("clock_out", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job case TimeTracking.clock_out(scope, job) do {:ok, _entry} -> {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket} end end @impl true def handle_info(:job_completed, socket) do job = Scheduling.get_job!(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job.id) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:job, job) |> load_checklist()} end def handle_info(:checklist_changed, socket), do: {:noreply, load_checklist(socket)} def handle_info(:tick, socket) do if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} end defp maybe_schedule_tick(socket) do if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) socket end defp assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job), do: job.cleaner_id == scope.user.id defp office_staff?(scope) do case scope.active_account_id do nil -> false account_id -> Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin] end end # Every job gets a checklist to complete through, even a trivially # empty one for a job nothing ever assigned a template to — lazily # instantiated here so `ChecklistComponent`'s completion flow (and # the invoice it triggers) is the one path every job completes # through, rather than a second one this view would otherwise need # for the no-checklist case. defp load_checklist(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job checklist = case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do nil -> {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, []) checklist checklist -> checklist end assign(socket, :checklist, checklist) end defp load_time_state(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job entries = TimeTracking.list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job) last_resolved = entries |> Enum.filter(&TimeEntry.resolved?/1) |> List.last() socket |> assign(:open_entry, TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job)) |> assign(:elapsed_seconds, TimeTracking.elapsed_seconds(scope, job)) |> assign(:last_worked_seconds, last_resolved && Earnings.worked_seconds(last_resolved)) |> assign(:earnings_cents, TimeTracking.job_earnings_cents(scope, job)) end defp client_name(%{client: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(%{property: %{client: %{name: name}}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(_job), do: "Job" defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-H:%M") defp format_duration(nil), do: "0m" defp format_duration(seconds) do hours = div(seconds, 3600) minutes = div(rem(seconds, 3600), 60) "#{hours}h #{minutes}m" end end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
4	  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
5	  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.
6	
7	  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
8	  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
9	  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
10	  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
11	  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
12	  payment link.
13	
14	  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
15	  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
16	  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.
17	
18	  ## Job completion integration point
19	
20	  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
21	  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
22	  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
23	  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
24	  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
25	  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
26	  """
27	
28	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
29	
30	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
31	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
32	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
33	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
34	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
35	
36	  ## Invoices
37	
38	  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
39	  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
40	    Invoice
41	    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
42	    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
43	    |> preload(job: :client)
44	    |> Repo.all()
45	  end
46	
47	  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
48	    Invoice
49	    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
50	    |> preload(job: :client)
51	    |> Repo.get!(id)
52	  end
53	
54	  @doc """
55	  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
56	  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
57	  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
58	  lookup has.
59	  """
60	  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
61	    Invoice
62	    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
63	    |> preload(job: :client)
64	    |> Repo.one()
65	  end
66	
67	  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
68	    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
69	    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
70	    |> Repo.insert()
71	  end
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
75	  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
76	  has a real caller.
77	
78	  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
79	  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
80	  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
81	  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
82	  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
83	  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
84	  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
85	  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
86	  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
87	  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
88	  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
89	  """
90	  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}
91	
92	  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
93	    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
94	  end
95	
96	  ## Payment collection
97	
98	  @doc """
99	  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
100	  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
101	  """
102	  def charge_card(
103	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
104	        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
105	      )
106	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
107	    invoice
108	    |> invoice_client()
109	    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
110	  end
111	
112	  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
113	    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}
114	
115	  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
116	    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)
117	
118	    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
119	           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
120	      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
121	    end
122	  end
123	
124	  @doc """
125	  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
126	  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
127	  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
128	  """
129	  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
130	    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
131	      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
132	    end
133	  end
134	
135	  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
136	    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
137	      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
138	      payment_method: payment_method,
139	      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
140	      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
141	    })
142	  end
143	
144	  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
145	  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
146	  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
147	  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
148	  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"
149	
150	  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
151	    Repo.transact(fn ->
152	      with {:ok, updated} <-
153	             invoice
154	             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
155	             |> Repo.update(),
156	           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
157	        {:ok, updated}
158	      end
159	    end)
160	    |> tap(fn
161	      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
162	      _error -> :ok
163	    end)
164	  end
165	
166	  @doc """
167	  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
168	  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
169	  """
170	  def create_payment_link(
171	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
172	        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
173	      )
174	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
175	    invoice
176	    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
177	    |> Repo.update()
178	  end
179	
180	  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
181	
182	  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
183	    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
184	  end
185	
186	  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
187	    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
188	    :ok
189	  end
190	
191	  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok
192	
193	  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
194	    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
195	    |> Payment.changeset(%{
196	      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
197	      status: status,
198	      provider: "stripe",
199	      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
200	      source: source
201	    })
202	    |> Repo.insert()
203	  end
204	
205	  ## Webhook
206	
207	  @doc """
208	  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
209	  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
210	  event data it can't trust.
211	  """
212	  def receive_webhook(conn) do
213	    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
214	      apply_webhook_event(event)
215	    end
216	  end
217	
218	  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
219	    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
220	      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
221	    end
222	  end
223	
224	  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
225	    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
226	      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
227	    end
228	  end
229	
230	  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}
231	
232	  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
233	    case object do
234	      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
235	        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)
236	
237	      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
238	        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)
239	
240	      _ ->
241	        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
242	    end
243	  end
244	
245	  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
246	    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
247	      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
248	      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
249	    end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts

  @impl Plug
  def call(conn, _opts) do
    if office_role?(conn.assigns.current_scope) do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),
    do: Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, scope.active_account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end
