defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Notification do
  @moduledoc """
  An outbound message — a client appointment reminder or a cleaner
  schedule-change alert — with delivery status and acknowledgment
  tracking.

  `kind: :reminder` notifications carry a `client_id` and move through
  `:sent -> :delivered | :undelivered -> :confirmed | :reschedule_requested`.
  `kind: :schedule_change` notifications carry a `cleaner_id` instead
  and move through `:pending -> :acknowledged` (or `:escalated` when
  never acknowledged in time).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @kinds [:reminder, :schedule_change]
  @channels [:email, :sms, :push]
  @statuses [
    :pending,
    :sent,
    :delivered,
    :undelivered,
    :failed,
    :confirmed,
    :reschedule_requested,
    :acknowledged,
    :escalated
  ]

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: :reminder | :schedule_change,
          channel: :email | :sms | :push,
          status: atom(),
          token: String.t() | nil,
          provider_message_id: String.t() | nil,
          failure_reason: String.t() | nil,
          change_summary: String.t() | nil,
          pushed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          sent_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          delivered_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          confirmed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          acknowledged_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          escalated_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "notifications" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: @kinds
    field :channel, Ecto.Enum, values: @channels
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: @statuses, default: :pending
    field :token, :string
    field :provider_message_id, :string
    field :failure_reason, :string
    field :change_summary, :string

    field :pushed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :sent_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :delivered_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :reschedule_requested_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :acknowledged_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :escalated_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id cleaner_id job_id kind channel status token provider_message_id
             failure_reason change_summary pushed_at sent_at delivered_at confirmed_at
             reschedule_requested_at acknowledged_at escalated_at)a

  def changeset(notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id, :kind, :channel, :token])
    |> unique_constraint(:token)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:job_id)
  end

  def kinds, do: @kinds
  def channels, do: @channels
  def statuses, do: @statuses
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

Replace cond with pattern matching.

Use with blocks over multiple nested conditionals.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 35ce3856: `CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate` had no
  UI to create one and no wiring to a job's checklist, so proof-of-work
  was unreachable through the live product without seeded data. No
  spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup %{conn: conn} do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client = ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Riverside Bungalow"})
    property = ClientsFixtures.property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "1 Main St"})

    conn = log_in_user(conn, user)

    %{conn: conn, scope: scope, client: client, property: property}
  end

  test "create_checklist_template supports sort/drop params and a blank property_id",
       %{scope: scope, property: property} do
    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => "",
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        }
      })

    assert template.property_id == nil
    assert length(template.items) == 2

    {:ok, updated} =
      Quality.update_checklist_template(scope, template, %{
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        },
        "items_drop" => ["1"]
      })

    assert updated.property_id == property.id
    assert length(updated.items) == 1
    assert hd(updated.items).task == "Wipe counters"
  end

  test "an empty-items create_checklist picks up the job's property template",
       %{scope: scope, client: client, property: property} do
    {:ok, _template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderSchedulerTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Regression test for issue 009fb5de: before the fix, an unconfigured
  Twilio adapter raised a `KeyError` out of `Delivery.Twilio.send_sms/2`
  instead of returning `{:error, _}`. That exception propagated out of
  `send_reminder/1` — never hitting the `{:error, _} -> send_email_reminder/2`
  clause — so an SMS-preferred client never got the email fallback, and
  `scan_and_send/1`'s `Enum.each` aborted every other due job in the
  same scan.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: false

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrm.{Accounts, ClientsFixtures, Notifications, Scheduling, UsersFixtures}
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderScheduler}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup do
    original_adapter = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, :sms_delivery_adapter)
    original_twilio_config = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, Delivery.Twilio, [])

    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, :sms_delivery_adapter, Delivery.Twilio)
    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, Delivery.Twilio, [])

    on_exit(fn ->
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, :sms_delivery_adapter, original_adapter)
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, Delivery.Twilio, original_twilio_config)
    end)

    :ok
  end

  test "an unconfigured Twilio adapter falls back to email instead of crashing the scan" do
    user = UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client =
      ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{
        name: "Jamie",
        email: "jamie-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
        phone: "+15555550101",
        preferred_channel: :sms
      })

    start_at = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 3600, :second)
    start_time = DateTime.to_time(start_at)

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
        status: :scheduled,
        scheduled_date: DateTime.to_date(start_at),
        start_time: start_time,
        end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
      })

    {:ok, _settings} = Notifications.update_reminder_settings(scope, %{lead_time_hours: 24})

    ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send()

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email)

    assert %Notification{channel: :email, status: :sent} =
             CleanerCrm.Repo.get_by!(Notification, job_id: job.id)
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.DataCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the setup for tests requiring
  access to the application's data layer.

  You may define functions here to be used as helpers in
  your tests.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      alias CleanerCrm.Repo

      import Ecto
      import Ecto.Changeset
      import Ecto.Query
      import CleanerCrmTest.DataCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Sets up the sandbox based on the test tags.
  """
  def setup_sandbox(tags) do
    pid = Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.start_owner!(CleanerCrm.Repo, shared: not tags[:async])
    on_exit(fn -> Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.stop_owner(pid) end)
  end

  @doc """
  A helper that transforms changeset errors into a map of messages.

      assert {:error, changeset} = Accounts.create_user(%{password: "short"})
      assert "password is too short" in errors_on(changeset).password
      assert %{password: ["password is too short"]} = errors_on(changeset)

  """
  def errors_on(changeset) do
    Ecto.Changeset.traverse_errors(changeset, fn {message, opts} ->
      Regex.replace(~r"%{(\w+)}", message, fn _, key ->
        opts |> Keyword.get(String.to_existing_atom(key), key) |> to_string()
      end)
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.Review

  @valid_attrs %{
    job_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
    client_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
    token: "review_token_123",
    status: :review_requested,
    review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
  }

  describe "changeset/2" do
    test "valid with just the request-side fields, no rating yet" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, @valid_attrs)
      assert changeset.valid?
    end

    test "requires job_id, client_id, and token" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, %{})
      refute changeset.valid?

      assert %{job_id: ["can't be blank"], client_id: ["can't be blank"], token: ["can't be blank"]} =
               errors_on(changeset)
    end

    test "rejects a rating outside 1..5" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, Map.put(@valid_attrs, :rating, 6))
      refute changeset.valid?
      assert %{rating: ["is invalid"]} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end

  describe "submission_changeset/2" do
    test "valid with a rating, text, status, and submitted_at" do
      changeset =
        Review.submission_changeset(%Review{}, %{
          rating: 5,
          text: "Great job!",
          status: :published,
          submitted_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        })

      assert changeset.valid?
    end

    test "requires rating, status, and submitted_at" do
      changeset = Review.submission_changeset(%Review{}, %{})
      refute changeset.valid?
      assert %{rating: ["can't be blank"], status: ["can't be blank"], submitted_at: _} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewRequestWorker do
  @moduledoc """
  On a job that's just been marked complete: sends the client an
  immediate thank-you note. Roughly 24 hours later — via the same
  Oban-cron scan pattern as
  `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler` — it also sends the
  actual review request, skipping any job that already has a review
  (or private complaint) on file so a visit is never asked for a
  second time.

  `perform/1` handles both triggers: an immediate one-off insert with
  `job_id` args (from `CleanerCrm.Reviews.request_review/1`, called
  right after job completion) sends the thank-you, while the cron
  plugin's empty-args invocation runs the periodic scan.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications

  import Ecto.Query
  require Logger

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.{Review, ReviewNotifier}

  @request_delay_seconds 24 * 60 * 60

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{"job_id" => job_id}}) do
    Job
    |> Repo.get(job_id)
    |> Repo.preload(:client)
    |> send_thank_you()

    :ok
  end

  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{}}) do
    scan_and_send()
    :ok
  end

  @doc "Enqueues the immediate thank-you note for a job that was just marked complete."
  def enqueue_thank_you(job_id) do
    %{job_id: job_id} |> new() |> Oban.insert()
  end

  @doc "Sends every review request that's due right now, across every account."
  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    now
    |> due_jobs()
    |> Enum.each(&send_request_isolated(&1, now))
  end

  defp send_thank_you(%Job{client: %Client{email: email}} = job) when is_binary(email) do
    ReviewNotifier.deliver_thank_you(job.client, job)
  end

  defp send_thank_you(_job), do: :ok

  # One job's send failing must never stop the rest of the scan — each
  # job gets its own failure boundary rather than the whole `Enum.each`
  # aborting on the first raise.
  defp send_request_isolated(job, now) do
    send_review_request(job, now)
  rescue
    error ->
      Logger.error(
        "ReviewRequestWorker failed to send review request for job #{job.id}: " <>
          Exception.format(:error, error, __STACKTRACE__)
      )
  end

  defp due_jobs(now) do
    already_reviewed = from r in Review, where: r.job_id == parent_as(:job).id
    cutoff = DateTime.add(now, -@request_delay_seconds, :second)

    from(j in Job,
      as: :job,
      where: j.status == :completed,
      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
      where: j.updated_at <= ^cutoff,
      where: not exists(already_reviewed),
      preload: [:client]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp send_review_request(%Job{} = job, now) do
    token = generate_token()

    %Review{account_id: job.account_id}
    |> Review.changeset(%{
      job_id: job.id,
      client_id: job.client_id,
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      status: :review_requested,
      token: token,
      review_request_sent_at: now
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()

    {:ok, _email} = ReviewNotifier.deliver_review_request(job.client, job, review_url(token))

    :ok
  end

  defp generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp review_url(token), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/reviews/#{token}"
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewRequestWorkerTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: false

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrm.{Accounts, ClientsFixtures, Repo, Scheduling, UsersFixtures}
  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.{Review, ReviewRequestWorker}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup do
    user = UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client =
      ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{
        name: "Jamie",
        email: "jamie-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
      })

    %{scope: scope, client: client}
  end

  defp completed_job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      attrs
      |> Enum.into(%{
        client_id: client.id,
        agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
        status: :completed,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -1),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })
      |> then(&Scheduling.create_job(scope, &1))

    job
  end

  test "enqueue_thank_you/1 sends the client an immediate thank-you", %{
    scope: scope,
    client: client
  } do
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

    ReviewRequestWorker.enqueue_thank_you(job.id)

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/thank/i)
  end

  test "scan_and_send/1 sends the review request once ~24h have passed and records it", %{
    scope: scope,
    client: client
  } do
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

    as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
    ReviewRequestWorker.scan_and_send(as_of)

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/review/i)
    assert %Review{status: :review_requested} = Repo.get_by!(Review, job_id: job.id)
  end

  test "scan_and_send/1 does not send before ~24h have passed", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
    completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

    ReviewRequestWorker.scan_and_send(DateTime.utc_now())

    refute_email_sent()
  end

  test "scan_and_send/1 skips a job that already has a review on file", %{
    scope: scope,
    client: client
  } do
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

    %Review{account_id: scope.active_account_id}
    |> Review.changeset(%{
      job_id: job.id,
      client_id: client.id,
      status: :review_requested,
      token: "already-sent-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
      review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()

    as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 48 * 60 * 60, :second)
    ReviewRequestWorker.scan_and_send(as_of)

    refute_email_sent()
  end

  test "scan_and_send/1 skips a job that was never completed", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
    {:ok, _job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        status: :in_progress,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -2),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 5 * 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
    ReviewRequestWorker.scan_and_send(as_of)

    refute_email_sent()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Reviews do
  @moduledoc """
  Post-visit review collection: an immediate thank-you plus a delayed
  review request after job completion
  (`CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewRequestWorker`), token-based public
  submission with a 1-5 star rating and free text, and the office's
  inbox over what comes back. A rating of 3 or below routes the
  submission to a private complaint for the owner instead of
  publication.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.{Review, ReviewRequestWorker}
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc "Enqueues the immediate post-completion thank-you for a job — see `ReviewRequestWorker`."
  def request_review(%Job{} = job), do: ReviewRequestWorker.enqueue_thank_you(job.id)

  @doc "Runs the periodic review-request scan now — see `ReviewRequestWorker`."
  defdelegate send_due_review_requests(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()),
    to: ReviewRequestWorker,
    as: :scan_and_send

  @doc "Creates a review directly, scoped to the caller's active account."
  def create_review(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Review{account_id: account_id}
    |> Review.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up a review by its public request token — no `Scope`, reached
  from an unauthenticated client's emailed link.
  """
  def get_review_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Review
    |> where([r], r.token == ^token)
    |> preload([:job, :client])
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc "The office's review inbox: every collected review and private complaint, most recent first."
  def list_reviews(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Review
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:job, :client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Records the client's star rating and text for a requested review. A
  rating of 4-5 publishes the review; 3 or below routes it to a
  private complaint for the owner instead.
  """
  def submit_review(%Review{} = review, rating, text) when rating in 1..5 do
    review
    |> Review.submission_changeset(%{
      rating: rating,
      text: text,
      status: visibility_for_rating(rating),
      submitted_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp visibility_for_rating(rating) when rating <= 3, do: :private
  defp visibility_for_rating(_rating), do: :published
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.ReviewsTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: false

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrm.{Accounts, ClientsFixtures, Reviews, Scheduling, UsersFixtures}
  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.Review
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup do
    user = UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client =
      ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{
        name: "Jamie",
        email: "jamie-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
      })

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        status: :completed,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -1),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    %{scope: scope, client: client, job: job}
  end

  test "create_review/2 scopes the review to the caller's active account", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    assert {:ok, review} =
             Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
               job_id: job.id,
               client_id: client.id,
               token: "tok-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
               status: :review_requested,
               review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
             })

    assert review.account_id == scope.active_account_id
  end

  test "get_review_by_token/1 finds a review with no scope needed", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    {:ok, review} =
      Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
        job_id: job.id,
        client_id: client.id,
        token: "findme-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    assert %Review{id: id} = Reviews.get_review_by_token(review.token)
    assert id == review.id
  end

  test "get_review_by_token/1 returns nil for an unknown token" do
    assert Reviews.get_review_by_token("nonexistent") == nil
  end

  test "list_reviews/1 lists only the account's own reviews, newest first", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    {:ok, older} =
      Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
        job_id: job.id,
        client_id: client.id,
        token: "older-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    {:ok, other_account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Other Co"})
    other_scope = %{scope | active_account_id: other_account.id, active_account: other_account}
    other_client = ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(other_scope, %{name: "Other Client"})

    {:ok, other_job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(other_scope, %{
        client_id: other_client.id,
        status: :completed,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -1),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    {:ok, _other_review} =
      Reviews.create_review(other_scope, %{
        job_id: other_job.id,
        client_id: other_client.id,
        token: "other-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    assert [%Review{id: id}] = Reviews.list_reviews(scope)
    assert id == older.id
  end

  test "submit_review/3 publishes a high rating", %{scope: scope, job: job, client: client} do
    {:ok, review} =
      Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
        job_id: job.id,
        client_id: client.id,
        token: "pub-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    assert {:ok, updated} = Reviews.submit_review(review, 5, "Wonderful!")
    assert updated.status == :published
    assert updated.rating == 5
    assert updated.text == "Wonderful!"
    assert updated.submitted_at
  end

  test "submit_review/3 routes a low rating to a private complaint", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    {:ok, review} =
      Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
        job_id: job.id,
        client_id: client.id,
        token: "priv-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    assert {:ok, updated} = Reviews.submit_review(review, 2, "Not great.")
    assert updated.status == :private
  end

  test "request_review/1 sends the immediate thank-you", %{job: job, client: client} do
    Reviews.request_review(job)

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/thank/i)
  end

  test "send_due_review_requests/1 runs the periodic scan", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
    Reviews.send_due_review_requests(as_of)

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/review/i)
    assert %Review{} = Reviews.get_review_by_token(review_token_for(scope, job))
  end

  defp review_token_for(scope, job) do
    scope
    |> Reviews.list_reviews()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.job_id == job.id))
    |> Map.fetch!(:token)
  end
end

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/thank/i)
  end

  test "send_due_review_requests/1 runs the periodic scan", %{
    scope: scope,
    job: job,
    client: client
  } do
    as_of = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
    Reviews.send_due_review_requests(as_of)

    assert_email_sent(to: client.email, subject: ~r/review/i)
    assert %Review{} = Reviews.get_review_by_token(review_token_for(scope, job))
  end

  defp review_token_for(scope, job) do
    scope
    |> Reviews.list_reviews()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.job_id == job.id))
    |> Map.fetch!(:token)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent do @moduledoc """ A job's checklist, grouped by room, with live progress and a gate on job completion until every required item is checked or explicitly skipped with a reason. "Still needed before this job is done" is recomputed from the checklist on every update, not cached from the last failed completion attempt — so it clears live the moment a cleaner checks off (or skips) the last required item, without needing to press "Finish Job" again. Skipping asks for a reason inline (its own `
`, scoped to that item) rather than hardcoding one; the reason is persisted on the `ChecklistItem` for `QualityLive.Review` to show the owner. Each item renders as its own `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent` so its before/after photo uploads stay independently scoped. Completing the job also generates its invoice, when `CleanerCrm.Billing` is present — read defensively per the moduledoc note on `CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job/2` about that hook not existing yet everywhere it's called from. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-------------------|----------|----------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | the checklist's job (for billing) | | checklist | `Checklist.t()` | yes | the job's checklist, items preloaded | Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :job_completed)` once the job is marked complete, so it can reload the job and checklist. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quality` - `CleanerCrm.Billing` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Billing alias CleanerCrm.Quality alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Checklist

{elem(@progress, 0)} of {elem(@progress, 1)}

{room}

    <.live_component :for={item <- items} module={ChecklistItemComponent} id={"checklist-item-#{item.id}"} current_scope={@current_scope} item={item} />

Still needed before this job is done:

  • {item.task}
<.button :if={is_nil(@checklist.completed_at)} data-test="mark-complete-button" phx-click="mark_complete" phx-target={@myself} class="mt-3" > Finish Job
""" end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:rooms, Quality.group_by_room(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:progress, Quality.progress(assigns.checklist)) |> assign(:incomplete, Quality.incomplete_required_items(assigns.checklist)) |> assign_new(:skip_form_item_id, fn -> nil end)} end @impl true def handle_event("mark_complete", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Quality.complete_job(scope, socket.assigns.checklist) do {:ok, _completed} -> maybe_generate_invoice(scope, socket.assigns.job) send(self(), :job_completed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, [])} {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :incomplete, incomplete)} end end def handle_event("show_skip_form", %{"item-id" => item_id}, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, item_id)} end def handle_event("cancel_skip_form", _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} end def handle_event("skip", %{"item-id" => item_id, "reason" => reason}, socket) do item = Enum.find(socket.assigns.checklist.items, &(&1.id == item_id)) case Quality.skip_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, item, reason) do {:ok, _item} -> send(self(), :checklist_changed) {:noreply, assign(socket, :skip_form_item_id, nil)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, socket} end end # Not every account has `CleanerCrm.Billing` wired to this hook yet # (see its moduledoc) — read defensively so this component never # needs to change again once it lands. defp maybe_generate_invoice(scope, job) do if Code.ensure_loaded?(Billing) and function_exported?(Billing, :generate_for_job, 2) do Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job) end end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout —
  # while the owner's review inbox is office-only, gated the same way
  # as the other office surfaces above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :reviews_office,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end
end

<.button phx-click="go" variant="primary">Send!</.button>
      <.button navigate={~p"/"}>Home</.button>
  """
  attr :rest, :global, include: ~w(href navigate patch method download name value disabled type)
  attr :class, :any
  attr :variant, :string, values: ~w(primary)
  slot :inner_block, required: true

  def button(%{rest: rest} = assigns) do
    variants = %{"primary" => "btn-primary", nil => "btn-primary btn-soft"}

    assigns =
      assign_new(assigns, :class, fn ->
        ["btn", Map.fetch!(variants, assigns[:variant])]
      end)

    if rest[:href] || rest[:navigate] || rest[:patch] do
      ~H"""
      <.link class={@class} {@rest}>
        {render_slot(@inner_block)}
      </.link>
      """
    else
      ~H"""
      <button class={@class} {@rest}>
        {render_slot(@inner_block)}
      </button>
      """
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Renders a confirmation dialog with Cancel + Confirm buttons.

  Replaces the legacy `data-confirm` pattern, which uses the native
  browser `window.confirm()` dialog. That dialog renders outside the
  DOM, so Vibium / Playwright / Wallaby can't observe or click it —
  every destructive action gated by it is silently un-testable.

  This component renders a DaisyUI `<dialog>` with two regular
  buttons, both clickable by browser automation. The dialog is
  hidden by default; trigger it from a sibling button's `phx-click`
  via `show_confirm("the-id")`.

  ## Example

      <button class="btn btn-error" phx-click={show_confirm("delete-client-\#{@client.id}")}>
        Delete
      </button>

      <.confirm_dialog
        id={"delete-client-\#{@client.id}"}
        title="Delete this client?"
        message="This cannot be undone."
        confirm_label="Delete"
        on_confirm={JS.push("delete-client", value: %{id: @client.id})}
      />

  Stable selectors for tests:
  - The trigger button — whatever the caller renders
  - `[data-role="confirm-cancel"]` inside the dialog
  - `[data-role="confirm-confirm"]` inside the dialog
  """
  attr :id, :string, required: true
  attr :title, :string, default: "Are you sure?"
  attr :message, :string, default: nil
  attr :confirm_label, :string, default: "Confirm"
  attr :cancel_label, :string, default: "Cancel"
  attr :confirm_class, :string, default: "btn btn-error"

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReviewLive.Public do @moduledoc """ The public, token-link review page a client reaches from their review-request email: a 1-5 star rating plus optional text, one-tap submission. A rating of 4-5 publishes the review; 3 or below routes it to a private complaint sent to the owner instead. Route: `/reviews/:token`. No login — reached from a mailed link, so it lives in the `:current_user` style `live_session` (mounts `current_scope` for the root layout without requiring one). ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Reviews` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Reviews alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.Review @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
This review link is invalid.
<.header>How was your cleaning?
<.button type="submit" data-test="submit-review-button" class="mt-2"> Submit Review
Thank you! Your review is on its way to being published.
Thanks for letting us know — we've sent your note directly to the owner.
""" end @impl true def mount(%{"token" => token}, _session, socket) do case Reviews.get_review_by_token(token) do nil -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: nil, rating: nil, submitted: false)} %Review{status: :review_requested} = review -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: review, rating: nil, submitted: false)} %Review{} = review -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: review, rating: review.rating, submitted: true)} end end @impl true def handle_event("set_rating", %{"rating" => rating}, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :rating, String.to_integer(rating))} end def handle_event("submit_review", %{"review" => params}, socket) do do_submit(socket, socket.assigns.submitted, socket.assigns.rating, params) end defp do_submit(socket, true, _rating, _params), do: {:noreply, socket} defp do_submit(socket, false, nil, _params) do {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "Please select a rating first.")} end defp do_submit(socket, false, rating, params) do case Reviews.submit_review(socket.assigns.review, rating, Map.get(params, "text")) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, review: updated, submitted: true)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "Something went wrong.")} end end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{user: user, scope: %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}}
  end

  # Regression for the accepted issue: completing a job with no agreed
  # price crashed invoice generation on the `invoices.amount_cents` NOT
  # NULL constraint. An unpriced recurring plan materializes visits
  # with no price (`CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), so
  # this drives that exact real-usage path end to end: create such a
  # plan, then complete the job it generated through the live UI.
  test "completing a plan-generated job with no agreed price completes without crashing and skips its invoice" do
    %{user: owner, scope: scope} = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client)

    {:ok, {_plan, [job]}} =
      Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
        property_id: property.id,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        occurrence_count: 1
      })

    refute job.agreed_price_cents

    conn = log_in_user(build_conn(), owner)
    {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{job.id}")

    job_live
    |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
    |> render_click()

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReviewLive.PublicTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp review_fixture(scope) do
    client =
      client_fixture(scope, %{
        name: "Jamie",
        email: "jamie-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
      })

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        status: :completed,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -1),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    {:ok, review} =
      Reviews.create_review(scope, %{
        job_id: job.id,
        client_id: client.id,
        token: "tok-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
        status: :review_requested,
        review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      })

    review
  end

  test "an invalid token shows an invalid-link notice", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, view, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/reviews/does-not-exist")
    assert has_element?(view, "[data-test='review-invalid-notice']")
  end

  test "a high rating publishes the review", %{conn: conn} do
    review = review_fixture(scope_fixture())

    {:ok, view, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/reviews/#{review.token}")

    view |> element("[data-test='review-rating-5']") |> render_click()
    view |> form("[data-test='review-form']", review: %{text: "Great!"}) |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(view, "[data-test='review-published-notice']")
  end

  test "a low rating routes to a private complaint, not publication", %{conn: conn} do
    review = review_fixture(scope_fixture())

    {:ok, view, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/reviews/#{review.token}")

    view |> element("[data-test='review-rating-2']") |> render_click()
    view |> form("[data-test='review-form']", review: %{text: "Not great."}) |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(view, "[data-test='review-private-notice']")
    refute has_element?(view, "[data-test='review-published-notice']")
  end
end

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

defmodule SexySpex do
  @moduledoc """
  Executable specifications for AI-driven development.

  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

  ## Technical Architecture

  SexySpex is built on top of ExUnit but provides a controlled execution environment
  specifically designed for AI-driven testing. Here's how it works:

  ### Core Architecture

  1. **ExUnit Foundation**: SexySpex uses ExUnit.Case under the hood for all test execution
  2. **Custom DSL**: Adds spex/scenario/given_/when_/then_ macros via SexySpex.DSL
  3. **Controlled Execution**: Only runs via `mix spex` command, never through `mix test`
  4. **Framework Helpers**: Provides SexySpex.Helpers for common patterns like app startup

  ### Execution Flow

  ```
  mix spex → Mix.Tasks.Spex → ExUnit.start() → Load spex files → ExUnit.run()
  ```

  ### Why Not Standard ExUnit?

  - **Compilation Control**: `mix spex` ensures proper compilation for complex dependency trees
  - **Application Lifecycle**: Better control over starting/stopping GUI applications
  - **AI-Optimized**: Manual mode, step-by-step execution, semantic helpers
  - **Cleaner Interface**: No confusion about tags, includes, or execution methods

  ### File Structure

  ```
  test/spex/
    hello_world_spex.exs     # Basic connectivity test
    user_workflow_spex.exs   # Complex user interactions
    screenshots/             # Generated screenshots
  ```

  ### Under the Hood

  When you write:
  ```elixir
  use SexySpex
  ```

  You get:
  ```elixir
  use ExUnit.Case, async: false  # Standard ExUnit test case
  import SexySpex.DSL               # spex/scenario/given_/when_/then_
  require Logger                # Logging support
  ```

  This means you have access to all standard ExUnit features:
  - `assert`, `refute`, `assert_raise`, etc.
  - `setup_all`, `setup` callbacks
  - `on_exit` for cleanup
  - Pattern matching in tests

  ### SexySpex vs ExUnit

  | Feature | SexySpex | ExUnit |
  |---------|------|--------|
  | Execution | `mix spex` only | `mix test` |
  | File Pattern | `*_spex.exs` | `*_test.exs` |
  | DSL | Given/When/Then | test/describe |
  | Target Use | AI-driven GUI testing | General testing |
  | Manual Mode | ✅ Built-in | ❌ Not available |
  | App Lifecycle | ✅ Helpers provided | Manual setup |
  | Error Log Detection | ✅ Automatic | ❌ Manual |

  ### Integration with Scenic Applications

  SexySpex provides special helpers for Scenic GUI applications:
  - `SexySpex.Helpers.start_scenic_app/2` - Start app with MCP server
  - `SexySpex.Helpers.can_connect_to_scenic_mcp?/1` - Test connectivity
  - `SexySpex.Helpers.application_running?/1` - Check app status

  This makes AI-driven GUI testing much simpler and more reliable.

  ## Basic Example

      defmodule MyApp.UserSpex do
        use SexySpex

        spex "user registration works" do
          scenario "successful registration" do
            given_ "valid user data", context do
              user_data = %{email: "test@example.com", password: "secure123"}
              assert valid_user_data?(user_data)
              {:ok, Map.put(context, :user_data, user_data)}
            end

            when_ "user registers", context do
              {:ok, user} = MyApp.register_user(context.user_data)
              assert user.email == "test@example.com"
              {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, user)}
            end

            then_ "user can login", context do
              assert {:ok, _session} =
                       MyApp.authenticate(context.user_data.email, context.user_data.password)
              {:ok, context}
            end
          end
        end
      end

  ## GUI Application Testing

  For GUI applications, use SexySpex.Helpers for easy setup:

      defmodule MyApp.GUISpex do
        use SexySpex

        setup_all do
          # Start GUI application with MCP server
          SexySpex.Helpers.start_scenic_app(:my_gui_app)
        end

        setup do
          # Reset state before each spex
          {:ok, %{timestamp: DateTime.utc_now()}}
        end

        spex "GUI interaction works" do
          scenario "application connectivity" do
            given_ "application is running", context do
              assert SexySpex.Helpers.application_running?(:my_gui_app)
              {:ok, context}
            end

            then_ "we can connect to MCP server", context do
              assert SexySpex.Helpers.can_connect_to_scenic_mcp?(context.port)
              {:ok, context}
            end
          end
        end
      end

  ## Running Spex

  SexySpex files can only be executed via the `mix spex` command:

      # Run all spex files
      mix spex

      # Run specific spex file
      mix spex test/spex/my_app_spex.exs

      # Run in manual mode (step-by-step)
      mix spex --manual

  **Important**: SexySpex files cannot be run via `mix test`. This ensures proper
  compilation and application lifecycle management for AI-driven testing.

  ## Error Log Detection

  SexySpex automatically captures error logs during test execution and fails the test
  if any errors are logged, even if no assertion failed. This catches:

  - GenServer crashes and terminations
  - FunctionClauseErrors and other runtime errors
  - Any `:error`, `:critical`, `:alert`, or `:emergency` level logs

  This is enabled by default. When errors are detected, you'll see output like:

      ❌ 2 error(s) logged during test execution:
        • [error] GenServer #PID<0.1234.0> terminating
        • [error] ** (FunctionClauseError) no function clause matching...

  ### Disabling Error Detection

  To disable error detection for a specific spex (e.g., when testing error handling):

      spex "error handling works", fail_on_error_logs: false do
        scenario "handles invalid input" do
          # This test expects errors to be logged
        end
      end

  ### Manual Error Capture

  You can also use the error capture module directly:

      # Start capturing
      SexySpex.ErrorCapture.start()
      SexySpex.ErrorCapture.clear()

      # ... do something ...

      # Check for errors
      if SexySpex.ErrorCapture.has_errors?() do
        IO.puts(SexySpex.ErrorCapture.format_errors())
      end

      # Get raw error list
      errors = SexySpex.ErrorCapture.get_errors()

  """

  @doc false
  defmacro __using__(opts) do
    quote do
      use ExUnit.Case, async: false
      import SexySpex.DSL
      require Logger

      @spex_opts unquote(opts)
    end
  end

  defmodule Helpers do
    @moduledoc """
    Common helper functions for spex files.

    These helpers provide reusable patterns for application startup,
    connectivity testing, and other common spex operations.
    """

    @doc """
    Starts a Scenic application with MCP server and waits for it to be ready.

    This helper handles the common pattern of:
    1. Ensuring compilation (needed for mix spex)
    2. Starting the application
    3. Waiting for MCP server
    4. Setting up cleanup

    ## Parameters
    - `app_name` - The application atom (e.g., `:quillex`)
    - `opts` - Optional configuration
      - `:port` - MCP server port (default: 9999)
      - `:timeout_retries` - Connection timeout retries (default: 20)

    ## Returns
    - `{:ok, context}` with app_name and port on success
    - Raises on failure

    ## Example
        setup_all do
          start_scenic_app(:quillex)
        end
    """
    def start_scenic_app(app_name, opts \\ []) do
      port = Keyword.get(opts, :port, 9999)
      timeout_retries = Keyword.get(opts, :timeout_retries, 20)

      # Ensure compilation (needed when running through mix spex)
      Mix.Task.run("compile")

      # Ensure all applications are started
      case Application.ensure_all_started(app_name) do
        {:ok, _apps} ->
          IO.puts("🚀 #{String.capitalize(to_string(app_name))} started successfully")

          # Wait for MCP server to be ready
          wait_for_mcp_server(port, timeout_retries)

          # Cleanup when tests are done
          ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit(fn ->
            IO.puts("🛑 Stopping #{String.capitalize(to_string(app_name))}")
            Application.stop(app_name)
          end)

          {:ok, %{app_name: to_string(app_name), port: port}}

        {:error, reason} ->
          IO.puts("❌ Failed to start #{String.capitalize(to_string(app_name))}: #{inspect(reason)}")
          raise "Failed to start #{String.capitalize(to_string(app_name))}: #{inspect(reason)}"
      end
    end

    @doc """
    Checks if we can connect to a Scenic MCP server on the given port.
    """
    def can_connect_to_scenic_mcp?(port) do
      case :gen_tcp.connect(~c"localhost", port, [:binary, {:active, false}]) do
        {:ok, socket} ->
          :gen_tcp.close(socket)
          true
        {:error, _reason} ->
          false
      end
    end

    @doc """
    Waits for MCP server to be ready with configurable retries.
    """
    def wait_for_mcp_server(port, retries \\ 20) do
      case can_connect_to_scenic_mcp?(port) do
        true ->
          IO.puts("✅ MCP server is ready on port #{port}")
          :ok
        false when retries > 0 ->
          Process.sleep(500)
          wait_for_mcp_server(port, retries - 1)
        false ->
          IO.puts("❌ MCP server failed to start on port #{port} after #{20 - retries} attempts")
          {:error, :mcp_server_timeout}
      end
    end

    @doc """
    Checks if an application is currently running.
    """
    def application_running?(app_name) do
      Application.started_applications()
      |> Enum.any?(fn {running_app, _, _} -> running_app == app_name end)
    end
  end

end
